name: Bob Marley and the Wailers
hook: The Kingston group that Lee Perry stripped down and Chris Blackwell repackaged as a rock album, which is how reggae reached the rest of the world.

blurb.age13: Bob Marley was born in 1945 in Nine Mile, a village in Saint Ann, Jamaica, and grew up partly in Trenchtown, a poor part of Kingston. In 1963 he formed the Wailers with Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer, and their first single, 'Simmer Down', was a ska hit in Jamaica. In 1970 the producer Lee 'Scratch' Perry recorded them with a bare, spare sound. In 1972 Chris Blackwell of Island Records signed them, and before releasing 'Catch a Fire' (1973) he added rock guitar and keyboards in London so that it would sell to rock fans. It worked. Marley was a Rastafarian, and his songs were about poverty, faith and political violence. In 1976 he was shot at his home in Kingston and survived. He died of cancer in 1981, aged 36.
blurb.adult: Born on 6 February 1945 in Nine Mile, Saint Ann, and raised partly in Kingston, Marley formed the Wailers in 1963 with Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer; 'Simmer Down', produced by Coxsone Dodd at Studio One with the Skatalites, was their first hit. Lee Perry produced 'Soul Rebels' (recorded August to November 1970, at Randy's, issued by Trojan) and its follow-up with the Barrett brothers as the rhythm section, a sparse sound of guitar, bass, drums, organ and voice that is often counted as the group's best work. Island signed them in 1972, and Blackwell remixed the Kingston sessions for 'Catch a Fire' (April 1973) at Basing Street with overdubs by the American guitarist Wayne Perkins and the keyboard player John Bundrick, thinning the bass-heavy mixes and packaging the record like a rock album. That decision is widely credited with taking Marley to a white rock audience, and it is the clearest case on this map of a label reshaping the sound of a record for a market. Clapton's cover of 'I Shot the Sheriff' was a US number one in 1974. Marley survived a shooting at his home in December 1976, played the One Love Peace Concert in 1978, where the rival party leaders Michael Manley and Edward Seaga shook hands on stage, and died in Miami on 11 May 1981. 'Legend' (1984) is the best-selling reggae album.

signatureTracks.title: Soul Rebel
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The Lee Perry sound: guitar, bass, drums, organ and voices, with nothing added.

signatureTracks.title: Concrete Jungle
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The first track on 'Catch a Fire', with the rock guitar overdub Island added in London.

signatureTracks.title: Redemption Song
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: His last album's closing song, just his voice and an acoustic guitar.
